stored_text.note: official.pdf is the 7-page scanned bill (cover letter, TBMM stamps, general justification, article justifications, bill text) with no text layer. I rendered the pages to images and read them; an English-model OCR gave a rough draft without Turkish diacritics, and the quotes below are transcribed from the page images, so they cannot be matched by script against a text layer. secondary.html is an English law-firm summary (Moroğlu Arseven), not a translation.

english_version.note: The stored secondary.html is an English summary by a law firm, not a translation. One web search found only Turkish news reports, no English text of the bill.

title.source_quote: 5237 sayılı ve 26/9/2004 tarihli Türk Ceza Kanunu ve Bazı Kanunlarda değişiklik yapılmasına dair kanun teklifim
title.why: original_title is the cover letter's description put in the title case Turkish uses for law titles, with 'teklifim' (my bill) made 'Teklifi'. The bill text itself is headed 'BAZI KANUNLARDA DEĞİŞİKLİK YAPILMASINA İLİŞKİN KANUN TEKLİFİ' (Bill on Amendments to Certain Laws), which the record does not mention. The English 'Bill Amending the Turkish Penal Code No. 5237 and Certain Laws' is accurate; the parenthetical '(artificial intelligence provisions, 2/3358)' is a descriptive addition. Quote transcribed from the page 1 image.

summary_claims.claim: Requires removal or blocking within six hours of AI content that violates personal rights, endangers public security or is a deepfake.
summary_claims.locator: PDF page 5, bill Article 3 (new paragraph 18 of Article 8 of Law No. 5651); transcribed from the page image
summary_claims.original_quote: "(18) Yapay zekâ sistemleri tarafından üretilen kişilik haklarına aykırı, kamu güvenliğini tehdit eden veya deepfake teknolojisi kullanılarak gerçek dışı şekilde düzenlenen içerikler hakkında erişim engelleme ve içerik kaldırma işlemleri 6 saat içinde yerine getirilir.
summary_claims.literal_translation: "(18) Access-blocking and content-removal measures concerning content produced by artificial intelligence systems that violates personality rights, threatens public security or has been edited in an unreal way using deepfake technology are carried out within 6 hours.

summary_claims.claim: Mandates a non-removable 'Generated by Artificial Intelligence' label on deepfakes (fines of TRY 500,000 to 5 million).
summary_claims.locator: PDF page 6, bill Article 7 (new Additional Article 5 of Law No. 5651); transcribed from the page image
summary_claims.original_quote: içeriğin kullanıcıya yapay olarak üretildiğine dair açık, anlaşılır ve silinemez bir ibare ile etiketlenmesi zorunludur. Bu ibare; “Yapay Zekâ Tarafından Üretilmiştir” ifadesiyle yer alır.
summary_claims.literal_translation: it is mandatory that the content be labelled for the user with a clear, understandable and non-erasable statement that it was produced artificially. This statement takes the form of the words 'Produced by Artificial Intelligence'.

summary_claims.claim: Sets provider duties (traceable training data, hallucination controls, human oversight).
summary_claims.locator: PDF page 6, bill Article 6 (new paragraph 3 of Article 7 of Cybersecurity Law No. 7545); transcribed from the page image
summary_claims.original_quote: a) Eğitim veri setlerinin şeffaflığı ve denetlenebilirliğini sağlamak, b) Yanlış ve manipülatif bilgi üretimini engelleyecek içerik doğrulama mekanizmaları kurmak, c) Hallüsinasyon riskini azaltacak algoritmik kontroller uygulamak,
summary_claims.literal_translation: a) Ensuring the transparency and auditability of training data sets, b) Establishing content-verification mechanisms that will prevent the production of false and manipulative information, c) Applying algorithmic controls that will reduce hallucination risk, [item d), not quoted for length: developing human-approved oversight mechanisms in high-risk applications]

key_terms.note: The bill says 'transparency and auditability' of training data sets. 'Traceable' is not in the bill; it comes from the law-firm summary ('transparent, traceable, and auditable'), which the register followed. The meaning is close, but the register should use the bill's terms.
Literally 'Produced by Artificial Intelligence'; 'Generated' is an equally good rendering of 'Üretilmiştir'.

The bill uses only the abbreviation BTK in its operative text; the article justification names 'Bilgi Teknolojileri ve İletişim Kurumu' (Information and Communication Technologies Authority). Bill Article 5 lets BTK issue urgent access-blocking decisions on AI content threatening public order or election security, with fines up to TRY 10 million.

issues: 'traceable training data' does not match the bill, which requires 'transparency and auditability' of training data sets; the word comes from the law-firm summary. The verification note says the article content was not read from the scan, and this is where that shows.

The bill text's own heading, 'Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına İlişkin Kanun Teklifi' (Bill on Amendments to Certain Laws), differs from the cover-letter wording used as original_title; the record could note both.
note: Every other content claim matches the scanned bill: the five laws amended (TCK 5237, 5651, 6698, 5809, 7545); the AI-system definition added to Law 5651 Art. 2; the user who directs an AI system to a criminal act deemed the perpetrator (new para. 6 of TCK Art. 125, the insult article, with the developer's penalty increased by half); six-hour removal with joint liability of content providers and developers; the label with BTK fines of TRY 500,000-5,000,000 and access blocking for systematic, intentional violations; BTK's urgent blocking power; provider duties with fines up to TRY 5 million. The bill has 11 articles. The scan can now be read for content; the verification note's statement that article content 'was not read from the scanned text' could be updated after a refresh.
